subject: Deployment mode risk triage & PoC asks
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Claire Jensen <c.jensen@pulsehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Deployment mode risk triage & PoC asks

Hi Claire — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can lock in the right PoC path for PulseHealth.

Recap of what I heard:
- Primary workloads: clinical note generation + templated responses (text-gen), occasional reranking for search.
- Expected steady-state: ~200 reqs/min during business hours with short bursts up to ~1200 reqs/min during batch processing windows.
- Data: PHI in prompts/outputs; retention policy ~30 days for logs, long-term model telemetry aggregated and non-PHI.
- Requirements: HIPAA controls, strong audit logs, KMS-managed keys, regional isolation (US), predictable p99 latency SLAs for key endpoints.
- Concern called out: "noisy neighbor" behavior on shared pools during peak hours causing latency spikes — team prefers predictable latency for clinical flows.

Qualifying questions (two quick asks so we pick the right deployment):
1) Do you require a customer-managed VPC / on-prem host for initial rollout, or would a Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pool in our VPC with network peering) be acceptable if we can meet SLA / KMS / audit requirements?
2) For the PoC, can you confirm the procurement contact and an approximate budget range (so we size the pilot and suggest a right-sized dedicated capacity)?

Proposed next step (expectation):
- 4-week dedicated-capacity PoC: reserved GPU pool sized for peak plus a fall-back plan to lower-cost hosted variants for non-critical traffic. During the PoC we’ll validate p99 latency at the endpoints you flagged and demonstrate KV/prefix caching benefits.

Attached: call recording (call-recording.mp3 link). I also attached an internal sketch of a dedicated capacity proposal to share with procurement once we confirm scope.

If you prefer a brief written decision tree instead of a full PoC I can put that together, but my recommendation from today's call is to run a short dedicated-capacity pilot because of the PHI and latency predictability needs.

Thanks — can you confirm procurement contact and whether VPC/isolation is a hard requirement?

— Logan
Logan Wright
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

From: Claire Jensen <c.jensen@pulsehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@pulsehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode risk triage & PoC asks

Hi Logan — great summary, thanks. A few quick answers below.

Short answers to your questions:
- VPC/on-prem: For initial rollout we prefer a VPC-peered Dedicated deployment (customer-controlled networking preferred). On-prem is not required for MVP but could be considered later.
- Procurement contact: procure@pulsehealth.com (cc'd). Budget: we have ~USD 75k–120k for a pilot depending on scope.

Additional context:
- Security: SOC2 + HIPAA controls are mandatory. We also need KMS integration and key separation policies.
- Traffic profile: median request ~150 tokens, p95 around 900 tokens for long reports. Peak timing is predictable (end-of-day batch jobs) which may create short noisy bursts.
- SLO expectations: p99 latency <= 250ms for quick clinical prompts; for long reports we accept higher latency but want predictable throughput.

Attached: pulse-technical-requirements.pdf (link) with our security checklist and sample traffic graphs.

Happy to jump on a technical deep-dive next week if Marissa/Ben are available.

Best,
Claire\Director of AI Integrations, PulseHealth
c.jensen@pulsehealth.com | +1 650-555-0123

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Claire's reply. Key points we need to act on:

1) VPC-peered Dedicated is preferred (customer-controlled networking). On-prem not needed for MVP.
2) Budget ~75k–120k for pilot, procurement contact provided.
3) Security: SOC2 + HIPAA + KMS key separation required.
4) Traffic: predictable end-of-day bursts; median token sizes small but long reports push p95.

Recommended immediate actions:
- Marissa: can you pull a Dedicated capacity configuration that meets 200 steady reqs/min and 1200 burst? Include p99 latency targets and proposed autoscale policy. Prioritize KV caching and prefix caching knobs to reduce p99 for quick prompts.
- Ben: prep a short PoC scope doc and an estimated price (within the budget band). Add clause for SLA verification and an escape hatch to hosted variants if throughput is overprovisioned during PoC.
- I'll schedule a technical deep-dive with Claire + Pulse security next Tue/Wed. Please let me know availability.

If either of you thinks we should push for a VPC appliance/on-prem option early, flag now — Claire indicated that is optional but they prefer VPC.

— Logan

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Deployment mode risk triage & PoC asks

Hi Claire — thanks for the fast answers and for looping procurement.

Plan proposal:
- PoC scope: 4-week Dedicated capacity pilot (VPC peering) focusing on the two critical endpoints you identified (clinical prompts + long reports). We will provision a reserved GPU pool sized for the 1200 bursts, include KMS integration and audit log forwarding to your SIEM.
- Success criteria: p99 latency <= 250ms for clinical prompts at expected token sizes; deterministic throughput handling for end-of-day batch windows; SOC2/HIPAA evidence checklist complete.
- Procurement path: Ben will send a scoped quote + short-term SOW to procure@pulsehealth.com by EOD Mon. Doc will reference HubSpot deal PH-2028-0142.
- Kickoff: proposed dates 2028-03-12 or 2028-03-15 for technical kickoff. Please confirm which works.

Attachments: redwood-dedicated-poc-scope.md (includes initial sizing table and monitoring checklist).

Next steps for Claire: confirm kickoff date and any additional regulatory evidence you need up-front. Once we have kickoff confirmed, Marissa will loop our infra team and security to collect the KMS/cert exchange details.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

— Ben Carter
